claims.text: Headline: Starmer's government implodes as students film themselves saying "we might die" before fatal bus crash
claims.note: Joins two unrelated stories; 'implodes' is figurative; the students' quote is misdescribed (see below). Rewritten.

claims.text: Subheadline: When the system's own children are laughing at death while the adults fight over who gets to lose next
Japanese students' bus crashed on the Banetsu Expressway (fatal)
claims.note: Jiji Press via Adnkronos, 7 May 2026: microbus carrying a high school soft tennis club crashed on the Ban-Etsu Expressway in Koriyama, Fukushima, on 6 May; a 17-year-old student died; driver, 68, arrested on suspicion of negligent driving resulting in death and injury.

claims.text: Students filmed themselves saying "we might die", not in terror but with casual nihilism / gallows humour
claims.note: Japanese report says a student on board sent a parent a message before the crash saying they might die (with video of the driving). Nothing supports 'laughing', 'nihilism' or 'gallows humour'. Single Japanese-language source; dropped from copy.

claims.text: NHK World caught the detail that Reuters missed
claims.note: No NHK World or Reuters report of the message found.

claims.text: Keir Starmer is fighting for his political life as his cabinet splits
claims.note: Al Jazeera, 12 May 2026 (URL slug 'starmer to face split cabinet as demands for his resignation mount'); about 80 Labour MPs had called for him to step down after local election losses.
Starmer was born in 1962 and became prime minister in July 2024 aged 61; he is not the youngest prime minister.

claims.text: The Financial Times reports he's 'weighing if his premiership can be saved' ahead of a cabinet meeting
claims.note: FT article republished on FT Chinese, 12 May 2026: 'Sir Keir Starmer is "weighing" if he can salvage his premiership ahead of a crucial cabinet meeting on Tuesday'; over 70 Labour MPs cited.

claims.text: Al Jazeera says the resignation demands are mounting
Starmer just won the biggest Labour landslide in decades
claims.note: Refers to the July 2024 general election, nearly two years earlier; not checked for this audit and 'just' is misleading. Dropped.

claims.text: Trump announced he'll suspend federal gas taxes, which he can't do without Congress, per the Associated Press
claims.note: AP via WTOP, 11 May 2026: 'Trump says he'll move to suspend federal gasoline tax. He can't do it on his own'; Congress would have to approve.

claims.text: Malaysia's fuel subsidy crisis we covered yesterday still festering
European stocks opened sharply lower as hopes for a US-Iran peace deal fade, according to CNBC
claims.note: CNBC's pre-market headline was 'European stocks to open lower as hopes for U.S.-Iran peace deal fade'; it did not say 'sharply'. Corrected wording.

claims.text: Bloomberg: Japan's ink shortage forcing potato chip manufacturers to print bags in black and white
claims.note: Bloomberg, 12 May 2026; syndicated text (ThePrint) names Calbee, which will temporarily use two ink colours on some products.

claims.text: SCMP: tokenized theater funding story from Hong Kong
claims.note: SCMP, 12 May 2026: 'Would you invest in a play? Hong Kong sets the stage for tokenised funding' (Esperanza Fintech Group).

claims.text: Times of India: a 'guess paper' leak derailed the NEET national exam, affecting millions of students
claims.note: Times of India site not reachable to confirm attribution. Business Today, 11 May 2026: Rajasthan SOG probing claims that questions worth 600 of 720 marks matched pre-exam material. The exam was cancelled on 12 May (https://scroll.in/latest/1092784/undergraduate-neet-2026-cancelled-after-alleged-paper-leak), possibly after this edition was generated. Copy attributes the probe to Business Today.

edits.headline: Starmer weighs whether his premiership can be saved
edits.subheadline: About 80 Labour MPs had called for the prime minister to step down after local election losses, Al Jazeera reported.
editorialBody: Prime Minister Keir Starmer was weighing whether he could save his premiership ahead of a cabinet meeting on Tuesday, the Financial Times reported. About 80 Labour MPs had called for him to step down after the party's local election losses, according to Al Jazeera.
President Trump said he would move to suspend the federal gasoline tax, the Associated Press reported. Congress would have to approve the change, the AP said.
European stocks were set to open lower as hopes for a US-Iran peace deal faded, CNBC reported.

A high school student aged 17 was killed when a microbus carrying his school's tennis club crashed on the Ban-Etsu Expressway in Koriyama, Fukushima, on 6 May, Jiji Press reported. Police arrested the driver on suspicion of negligent driving.
Japan's biggest potato chip maker, Calbee, will print some bags in two colours because of an ink shortage, Bloomberg reported.
Police in Rajasthan were investigating whether questions in India's NEET medical entrance exam matched material shared before the test, Business Today reported.
A Hong Kong firm was using tokenised funding to finance a stage play, the South China Morning Post reported.
